Name: De Morgan implementations
Description:
Inversion circle pushed backward (Bubble pushing)
- Begin at the output of the circuit and work toward the inputs.
- Push any bubbles on the final output back toward the inputs so that you can read an equation in terms of the output (for example, Y) instead of the complement of the output (-Y).
- Working backward, draw each gate in a form so that bubbles cancel. If the current gate has an input bubble, draw the preceding gate with an output bubble. If the current gate does not have an input bubble, draw the preceding gate without an output bubble.
Only NAND implementation: Use SOP (AB+BC+CD = -((-(AB))(-(BC))(-(CD))))
Only NOR implementation: Use POS ((A+B)(B+C)(C+D) = -(-(A+B)+(-(B+C))+(-(C+D))))
BEWARE: INVERT SINGLE LITERAL e.g. A to -A

- Inputs are on the left (or top) side of a schematic.

- Whenever possible, gates should flow from left to right.
- Straight wires are better to use than wires with multiple corners (jagged wires waste mental effort following the wire rather than thinking of what the circuit does)
- Wires always connect at a T junction.
- A dot where wires cross indicates a connection between the wires.
- Wires crossing without a dot make no connection

Name: Sequential timing
Description:
Aperture time around clock edge -> Discrete units of clock cycles, clock period must be long enough for all signals to settle
inputs: t_setup (stabilized during setup time), t_hold (stabilized for at least some hold time), both makes up aperture time of circuit
outputs: t_ccq: clock to Q contamination delay, t_pcq: clock to Q propagation delay
(T_c: Clock period or cycle time, f_c=1/T_c: Clock frequency)
The dynamic discipline states that the inputs of a synchronous sequential circuit must be stable during the setup and hold aperture time around the clock edge. By imposing this requirement, we guarantee that the flip flops sample signals while they are not changing. 
T_skew as clock skew time, treated as a burden (Usually a clock tree from central clock, branch to each hierarchy due to time latency)

Name: Setup time constraint
Description: t_pcq + t_pd + t_setup + t_skew <= T_c (t_pcq+t_setup: sequencing overhead)

Name: Hold Time constraint
Description: t_ccq + t_cd >= t_hold + t_skew

Name: Metastability
Description:
During aperture time, resolution titme to reach stable state is unbounded
Outside aperture time: t_res = t_pcq, Inside aperture time t_res can be longer and happens random
Propability resolution time t_res exceeds some arbitrary time t: P(t_res > t)=T_0/T_c*e^(-t/\t), T_0/T_c: Probability input changes at a bad time (during aperture time), \t a time constant how fast flipflop moves away from metastable state (delay through cross-coupled gates in flip flop)

Name: Erasable PROM (EPROM)
Description:
usually thousands write cycle, erased with UV light and reprogrammed
Erasable PROMs replace the PROM transistor and fuse with a floating-gate transistor (not physically attached to any other wires). When suitable high voltages are applied, electrons tunnel through an insulator onto the floating gate, turning on the transistor and connecting the bitline to the wordline (decoder output). Exposed to intense ultraviolet (UV) light for about half an hour, the electrons are knocked off the floating gate, turning the transistor off.
